studies.title: The Cave And The Ornament
studies.meaning: The surah opens with praise for a Book that has no crookedness in it, straight and confirming, sent to warn and to give good news. Then two hard sentences: the messenger is told he may destroy himself with grief over people who will not believe, and the world is described as an ornament placed on the earth to test which of them acts best, before being stripped to bare ground. Then the youths in the cave appear, introduced as something less remarkable than the reader assumes.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. Classical sources report with broad agreement that the Meccan leadership sent to the scholars of Medina for questions to test the message, and were given three: the sleepers in the cave, a traveller who reached the ends of the earth, and the spirit. This surah answers the first two and the third comes at the end of the preceding surah. The reports differ on details but agree on the shape.

keyTerms.note: A word for a bend in something that should be straight, used of a stick or a road. Denying it of the Book at the very first ayah sets up the surah, which is about things that look bent until explained.
Decoration added to a thing rather than belonging to it, like jewellery on a person. Applied to everything on earth, it makes the world's attraction real and also removable, which the next ayah does.
A rare and violent word for killing yourself by grief or effort, used of an animal driven past exhaustion. It measures how heavily the refusal of others was being felt.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Caves were shelter of the last resort in that landscape: cool, defensible, and used by shepherds, fugitives and travellers caught out after dark. Everyone knew one. The story the surah is about to tell concerned young men who took refuge from a ruler in exactly such a place, so the setting needed no explaining. What needed explaining was why God would find it unremarkable.
studies.didYouKnow: The surah's opening ayat contain a rare pause mark in the standard printed text, placed after the word for crookedness, which prevents a reciter from joining it to the word that follows and reversing the sense. It is one of only a handful of such marks in the whole Quran. Reciting this surah on Fridays is a long-established practice.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The seventh ayah sets the terms for everything the surah will narrate. The world's attractiveness is not an illusion and not a trap; it is described as a deliberate arrangement whose purpose is to find out which of them is best in conduct. That makes ordinary life the examination rather than a distraction from it. The eighth ayah then removes the ornament, which places the test inside a frame the person taking it can see.

crossReferences.why: Names the same purpose for death and life: to test which of you is best in deed.
Returns to the same image later in the surah, water and then wealth as ornament.
Uses a similar phrase about grieving yourself to death over those who will not believe.

studies.applyIt: Look at one thing in your home you saved for and now barely see. Not to feel guilty about it: just register that the wanting was more vivid than the having. The surah calls the world an ornament and means it as a description of how attraction works, not as a warning against owning things. Notice the pattern once and it stays noticeable.

studies.title: Unless God Wills
studies.meaning: A prohibition on a way of speaking, not on planning. Do not say of anything that you will do it tomorrow, without adding that it is subject to God's will. Then two supports are given: remember your Lord if you forget, which the commentators read either as saying the phrase late or as remembering God generally; and a modest hope that He may guide you nearer to what is right. The third ayah returns to the sleepers and states their number of years.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The classical sources report, with reasonable agreement, that the questions put to test the message went unanswered for a period after a promise to answer the next day, and that these ayat came in connection with that delay. The reports vary in detail. The surah then places the instruction directly before a statement of the sleepers' exact duration, which reads as a quiet demonstration of who knows what.

keyTerms.note: The ordinary word for the next day. Its plainness is the point: the prohibition is not about grand plans but about the smallest and most confident unit of the future a person uses.
The verb covers both losing something from memory and neglecting it. Building an allowance for forgetting into the instruction itself keeps the phrase from becoming a test a person can fail.

A word for maturity of judgement, used of a young person old enough to manage property. It names the good outcome as competence rather than as fortune, which fits a surah full of people learning what they did not understand.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Nothing about tomorrow was reliable. A caravan's arrival depended on weather, raiders and the health of animals; a harvest depended on rain that either came or did not; a person could be well in the morning and dead by evening of a fever nobody could name. Promises were made with hedges built in, and everyone had watched a confident plan collapse. The instruction attached a name to a caution people already felt.
studies.didYouKnow: The number of years is given in an unusual way: three hundred years, and they added nine. Commentators have long noted that three hundred solar years correspond almost exactly to three hundred and nine lunar years, which is the calendar the addressees used. The surah gives the figure and then immediately says to leave the knowledge of it to God.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The instruction is about the grammar of a sentence and reaches something larger. Saying you will do something tomorrow asserts a small ownership of the future, and the correction does not remove the plan; it adds a clause. What that clause does is keep intention and outcome in separate hands, which is what allows a person to plan seriously without being destroyed when the plan fails. The permission to say it late is mercy built into the same instruction.

crossReferences.why: Names what no one knows, including what a soul will earn tomorrow.
Jacob gives his sons practical instructions and then hands the judgement back to God.
Immediately before this, the same surah refuses to settle a disputed number.

studies.applyIt: Say the phrase out loud once today, in English or in Arabic, about something small and near: the appointment this afternoon, the meal you are cooking. Not as a superstition and not as a hedge. Just notice what it does to the sentence, and to you, to attach a condition to something you had assumed was settled.

studies.title: Stay With Those Who Call
studies.meaning: The instruction is to hold yourself with a particular group, and the verb is the one for patience, so staying is presented as something that requires endurance. Those described are people who call on their Lord at the two ends of the day, wanting His face and nothing else. Then the eyes are addressed again, told not to pass over them in search of the world's glitter. The last clause warns against following someone whose priorities have come apart.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. Classical reports connect the ayah with a request from leading men of Quraysh that the poor believers, several of them former slaves, be kept away from the gatherings before they would sit and listen. The reports vary in detail, and the commentators generally accept the substance. The instruction answers by reversing the request: stay with those men, and do not look past them.

keyTerms.note: The verb for patience made transitive, so it is not be patient but restrain yourself and keep yourself in place. It concedes that remaining in that company may take effort.
The word for a face, used in the Quran for God's own self and for what is turned towards. Naming it as the object of desire rules out every secondary motive without listing them.

A rare word for something that has run ahead of itself or been squandered. The commentators read it of a life whose affair has slipped past all measure, so the man is not described as wicked but as unmoored.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Who sat with whom was public information in Mecca and carried real weight. An assembly had an order, and a man of standing did not share a mat with a client or a freed slave without it being noticed and discussed. Several of the earliest believers were exactly such men, bought out of ownership or disowned by their families. The instruction to stay with them was an instruction about seating.
studies.didYouKnow: The same word for the world's ornament used at the start of this surah returns here, now as something the eyes might drift towards. The surah uses it three times in different settings, which is one of the ways it holds together. A very similar instruction appears in an earlier surah, where the reason given is that those people call on their Lord morning and evening.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The ayah locates worth in a practice rather than in a person's standing, and then asks the reader to organise his attention accordingly. What makes the group worth staying with is named precisely: they call on their Lord, at both ends of the day, wanting nothing but Him. Nothing is said about their learning, their manners or their usefulness. And the warning at the end is not about a bad man but about a heart made heedless, which is a condition rather than a verdict.

crossReferences.why: Gives the same instruction in almost the same words, with a warning against driving them away.
A whole passage correcting attention given to the influential over a blind man who came seeking.
Repeats the instruction about the eyes and adds the same command about the wing.

studies.applyIt: Think about who you would text if something good happened this week, and who you would text if something bad did. If the two lists are different, notice why. Then this week arrange to spend an hour with someone from the second list who has nothing to offer you except that you are better around them. That is what this ayah is describing.
